**Continuous 2.16.3**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.16.3.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.16.3.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.16.3.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.16.3.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.16.3.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.16.3.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.16.3.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.16.3-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.16.3.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.16.3-vscode/continuous-cli-2.16.3.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.16.2

IDGAF now means what its chip says: at IDGAF nothing is denied or asked, including rules you set as Never, and what would have objected is recorded and counted instead. OpenRouter's model information now refreshes automatically by default, which reverses a 2.16.0 promise; it can be turned off. The model's thinking shows again while it streams, and cost, context, reasoning and prompt cache stay visible under the prompt.

### Behaviour changes

- **IDGAF no longer denies or asks about anything, including rules you set as Never.** At IDGAF the permission layer lets every tool call through: Never (`deny`) and always-on (`floor`) rules, the CLI's `exclude` lists and `--exclude`, protected paths and secret files, the safety floor, commands that hide what they run, writes to paths built at run time, the locked policy and configuration files, the tainted-session rule and changed MCP tool definitions no longer stop a call, and nothing waits for an answer. In `cn -p` and `cn serve`, tools that ask or are excluded are offered at IDGAF, and a loop worker of an `--auto` parent runs at the parent's levels. What would have stopped each call is recorded in its decision and in the audit trail, never shown to the model. A tool you switched off, Plan mode, an `--agent` file's tool list, a subagent's limits and hooks you wrote yourself still apply. Below IDGAF nothing changed.

- **OpenRouter's model list is now refreshed automatically, by default. This reverses the 2.16.0 privacy promise** that `openrouter.ai` is contacted only when you choose Pull now or Refresh. With the new setting **Model information updates** on **Automatic** (the default), Continuous downloads OpenRouter's public model list (names, context sizes, per-token prices for cost estimates and `--max-budget-usd`, tool support) in the background whenever the copy on this computer is missing or older than 24 hours: about 15 to 60 seconds after the IDE starts, 1 to 3 seconds after the terminal agent starts, and again once a day while it runs. This happens even if you do not use OpenRouter. The request is one GET to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` with no key, account, prompt or body, and only `accept` and `user-agent: continuous` headers; nothing waits for it, failures are retried with backoff (5 minutes up to 6 hours) and the list you had stays in use. Provider setup no longer asks "Pull the latest model information from OpenRouter?" in Automatic mode; the model step, the Models settings page and the console's Total Usage show "OpenRouter model information last updated <time> · Refresh now".
  - **To turn it off**: set `continuous.modelInformationUpdates` to `off` in VS Code (or choose Off on the Models settings page), or add `modelCatalog: off` to `~/.continuous/config.yaml` (read by JetBrains and the terminal agent too), or set `CONTINUOUS_MODEL_INFO_UPDATES=off`. Off never contacts `openrouter.ai` and uses the bundled model data. **Only when I ask** (`modelCatalog: manual`) keeps the 2.16.0 behaviour. If you chose "Don't ask again" in 2.16.0 or 2.16.1 (`modelCatalog: never`), nothing changes for you: no background refresh and no question. The interval is `continuous.modelInformationRefreshHours` / `modelCatalogRefreshHours` (default 24).
  - `continuous models refresh` is refused when updates are off.
  - **Ollama is unchanged**: `ollama.com` is still contacted only when you choose Download or Refresh in Ollama's setup, never at start-up or on a timer, and the new setting does not apply to it.
  - Firewall and sandbox allowlists: expect `openrouter.ai` (TCP 443) shortly after start-up on a machine whose list is missing or stale.

### New

- **See how often IDGAF ran past an objection.** Each call IDGAF let through past a rule or guard is recorded in the audit trail with what would have stopped it (masked). The Permissions page's audit overview says how many calls IDGAF ran in the last 30 days, `cn` prints one line at the end of a run, and the stream-json `result` event carries `numIdgafObjections`. The model never sees the count, and a failing audit trail never blocks a call.
- **IDGAF lasts for the editor session.** In VS Code, IDGAF survives a reload of the chat panel and an extension host restart; a new editor session or window starts at your saved levels, because `permissions.yaml` never stores IDGAF. JetBrains starts the panel at the saved levels. In `cn`, a resumed loop follows the levels of the process that resumes it, not the ones saved with the session.

### Fixes

- **The model's thinking shows again, live.** Claude Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos return their thinking empty unless asked, so the chat showed nothing until the answer; requests to them (on Anthropic's API and on Bedrock) now ask for summarized thinking (`thinking.display: "summarized"`, billed the same as the hidden thinking), including with reasoning off on the models that think anyway. Gemini 2.5 and later are asked for their thought summaries, which arrive as thinking rather than as part of the answer. OpenAI's reasoning summaries no longer appear twice. In the chat, thinking streams open and follows the newest text while the model thinks, then folds to one line, "Thought for 4.2s", that opens it again; the new **Keep Thinking Expanded** user setting (`ui.keepThinkingExpanded`) leaves it open. Later turns send Anthropic's API the same conversation as before (the summaries are not sent back); on Bedrock, which already sent thinking blocks back, they now carry the summary the model returned instead of empty text.

- **Cost, context, reasoning and prompt cache stay visible under the prompt.** They were behind a "..." button at every width. They are now in the row under the prompt at every width: as the row narrows the labels shorten and the model name truncates, but the numbers stay. The usage details open with a click or Enter instead of on hover, model tips are a button with a count, and the "..." button is gone.
- The IDGAF chip's tooltip and screen-reader description are shortened to "Every rule is ignored." and how to go back to Careful.

### Docs and internal

- The permissions page says how long IDGAF lasts in the extension and in `cn` and where the would-have-objected count is shown; `PRIVACY.md`, the OpenRouter provider page and the `config.yaml` reference (`modelCatalog`) describe the automatic refresh and how to turn it off.
- Tests that call a paid model API now run only with `RUN_LIVE_PROVIDER_TESTS=1`; without it, test setup removes provider credentials from the environment. See "Live provider tests" in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
